name: missing ; (next line is print)
eb_msg: Expected ';' at the end of the statement.
eb_sugg: Add a semicolon after '10'.

name: missing ; (blank line + comment after)
eb_msg: Expected ';' at the end of the statement.
eb_sugg: Add a semicolon after '10'.

name: missing ; (next line is assignment)
eb_msg: Expected ';' at the end of the statement.
eb_sugg: Add a semicolon after '10'.

name: missing ; on last statement
eb_msg: Expected ';' at the end of the statement.
eb_sugg: Add a semicolon after 'b'.

name: missing )
eb_msg: Missing ')' to close the '(' opened on line 2.
eb_sugg: Add ')' after '4'.

name: missing ) (expression split over lines)
eb_msg: Missing ')' to close the '(' opened on line 2.
eb_sugg: Add ')' after '4'.

name: extra )
eb_msg: Found an extra ')' that has no matching '('.
eb_sugg: Remove the extra ')' or add a matching '(' earlier.

name: two operators in a row
eb_msg: Two operators in a row: '+' followed by '*'.
eb_sugg: Remove one of them, or put a number or variable between them.

name: operator with no right operand
eb_msg: The operator '+' has no value on its right side.
eb_sugg: Add a number or variable after '+', or remove the '+'.

name: missing operator between values
eb_msg: Missing operator between 'a' and 'b'.
eb_sugg: Put an operator such as '+' or '*' between them, or end the statement with ';'.

name: missing value after =
eb_msg: Missing value after '='.
eb_sugg: Write a value after '=', for example 'x = 5;'.

name: empty parentheses
eb_msg: Empty parentheses '()' are not allowed.
eb_sugg: Put an expression inside them, for example '(a + 1)'.

name: undeclared variable
eb_msg: Variable 'marks' has not been declared.
eb_sugg: Declare it using 'int marks = 0;' before this line.

name: misspelled variable
eb_msg: Variable 'scroe' has not been declared.
eb_sugg: Did you mean 'score'? If 'scroe' is a new variable, write 'int scroe = ...;'.
gcc_msg: ‘scroe’ undeclared (first use in this function); did you mean ‘score’?

name: misspelled print keyword
eb:
int x = 3;
prnt x;
c:
int x = 3;
prinft("%d\n", x);
eb_msg: Unknown word 'prnt'.
eb_sugg: Did you mean the keyword 'print'? Keywords are lowercase and followed by a space.
gcc_msg: implicit declaration of function ‘prinft’; did you mean ‘printf’? [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]

name: duplicate declaration
eb_msg: Variable 'age' has already been declared (on line 1).
eb_sugg: Use a different variable name, or assign a new value with 'age = ...;'.

name: variable used in its own declaration
eb:
int a = a + 1;
print a;
c:
int a = a + 1;
printf("%d\n", a);
eb_msg: Variable 'a' is used in its own declaration, before it has a value.
eb_sugg: Give it a starting value that does not use 'a', for example 'int a = 0;'.

name: division by literal 0
eb_msg: Division by zero. You are dividing by the number 0.
eb_sugg: Make sure the value on the right of '/' is not zero.

name: division by a variable that is 0
eb_msg: Division by zero. Variable 'zero' is 0 at this point, so dividing by it is impossible.
eb_sugg: Make sure the value on the right of '/' is not zero.

name: division by an expression that is 0
eb:
int a = 8 / (4 - 4);
print a;
c:
int a = 8 / (4 - 4);
printf("%d\n", a);
eb_msg: Division by zero. The expression on the right of '/' works out to 0.
eb_sugg: Make sure the value on the right of '/' is not zero.

name: arithmetic overflow
eb:
int big = 2000000000 * 2;
print big;
c:
int big = 2000000000 * 2;
printf("%d\n", big);
eb_msg: The result of '*' here is too large to fit in an int.
eb_sugg: Use smaller numbers. An int must be between -2147483648 and 2147483647.
gcc_msg: integer overflow in expression of type ‘int’ results in ‘-294967296’ [-Woverflow]

name: literal too large for int
eb:
int n = 99999999999;
print n;
eb_msg: The number 99999999999 is too large. An int can be at most 2147483647.
eb_sugg: Use a smaller number.
gcc_msg: overflow in conversion from ‘long int’ to ‘int’ changes value from ‘99999999999’ to ‘1215752191’ [-Woverflow]

name: unknown symbol
eb_msg: Unknown symbol '@'. ErrorBuddy only understands letters, digits and + - * / = ( ) ;
eb_sugg: Remove the symbol or replace it with one of the supported symbols.

name: name starts with a digit
eb:
int 2nd = 5;
print 2nd;
c:
int 2nd = 5;
printf("%d\n", 2nd);
eb_msg: '2nd' is not a valid name. Variable names cannot start with a digit.
eb_sugg: Start the name with a letter, for example 'value1' instead of '1value'.
